description: OS-neutral lock port. Callers (Node facade, Rust crate, hook) see only these operations; the fd or job handling lives in the driver.

fields.name: registry lock name (packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json)
fields.path: absolute path of the lock file, created once and never removed while the resource lives

fileRules: opened O_RDWR (NFSv4 and BSD refuse an exclusive lock on a read-only fd)
the description is always FD_CLOEXEC except inside exactly one spawn that borrows it, through an explicit fd mapping
after acquire, fstat(fd).ino must equal stat(path).ino; otherwise close and retry
release and borrower close only; nobody calls LOCK_UN on any copy of a description

killWaitMs.meaning: upper bound on waiting for a predecessor domain that was already killed to be signaled; never a wait-for-drain

acquire.rule: returns acquired only when BOTH hold: the kernel lock is held AND the predecessor domain recorded next to the lock file is empty (predecessor.v1.json). A free kernel lock alone is not proof.

release.rule: the holder releases only after its own domain is empty (run_borrowed already waited for the child, killed leftovers and waited for empty). Release closes every copy of the description it owns.

run_borrowed.rule: the only way a child command passes with the holder's authority. Hands the description to exactly one child through an explicit fd mapping (default slot 3, env FGOS_LOCK_FD=<name>:3). When argv[0] is git, the call prepends -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false. After the child exits: kill what is left in the domain, wait for the domain to be empty, only then return.

probe.rule: non-blocking LOCK_SH attempt that never obstructs another holder; the shared lock is dropped at once.

holders.notes: Linux scans /proc/*/fdinfo/* for a lock: line on the inode of the lock file. macOS and Windows-without-helper report unlistable.

input.path: directory the lock files live in

held.domain: present only for predecessor-domain-not-empty: the predecessor domain record (predecessor.v1.json)

invariants: timeout and held never leave a description open: the lock is released before the result is returned
predecessor-domain-not-empty is returned after the lock was released again
no result of any operation is ever derived from a pid, a TTL or an mtime

levelMeaning.kernel: enforced by the kernel and measured on a real machine
levelMeaning.kernel-unmeasured: kernel semantics expected, no measurement yet
levelMeaning.job-scoped: enforced through a job/helper process plus the predecessor rule (Windows driver)
levelMeaning.unsupported: the driver does not provide it; the caller must not rely on it
levelMeaning.none: no guarantee (network filesystem); the driver refuses the lock with a named error

guarantee.containment: macOS holder-lock containment is best-effort and is reported in notes, not in a level
